items.q: What does Picard mean by "energy is the potential for change"?
items.a: Energy is **flow and transformation**, not a quantity you eat. "The difference between a living person and a cadaver is the **flow of energy**." Think in verbs — you are an **energy transformation being**.

No — they are **energy patterning and distribution systems** that link psychology, behavior, and organ-specific aging. "They act as antennas to link your **psychological experiences** to your organ health."

items.q: How is the daily energy budget split?
items.a: Three buckets: **vital costs** (heart, brain, detox), **stress costs** (sympathetic activation, worry, cortisol), and **GMR** (growth, maintenance, repair). Chronic stress **steals from GMR**; sleep and meditation reallocate toward repair.

Detox steals ~**10% of your energy budget**, disrupts sleep, and mitochondrial-disease patients are often intolerant. "Are you willing to sacrifice **10% of your energy budget** going towards alcohol detoxification?"

items.q: Why do you feel apathetic when sick?
items.a: **Sickness behavior** — the immune system expands its energy share; the body conserves via pain, cold, anorexia, and apathy (~**10–15% digestion cost** saved).

Life requires **resistance to transform energy** (exercise, learning, breath-hold). Too much = suffering; too little = atrophy (**astronaut model**). Fear can signal something there that can help you grow.

items.q: Why can't you just eat more for more energy?
items.a: Obesity/lethargy is often **dysfunctional transformation and distribution**, not lack of input. Energy directed to an organ builds **mitochondrial capacity** there — finite budget creates trade-offs (amenorrhea, overtraining).
Picard lab: same-genome hairs **gray and re-darken** with stress cycles — reversible depigmentation linked to stress timing (**gray-hair stress reversal**).

items.q: Does life purpose show up in brain mitochondria?
items.a: Post-mortem **DLPFC mitochondria** correlate with life purpose and social connection. ~**90% of longevity is non-genetic** (~7% heritable); mitochondrial DNA is **100% maternal inheritance**.
Tissue-specific **mitochondrial types** from one maternal lineage — genes identical across cells, but mitotypes differ by organ (mitoypeexplorer.org from the Picard lab).

items.q: What lifestyle levers actually move the needle?
items.a: Sleep (**10–15% energy savings**, parasympathetic restoration); expert meditators ~**−40% metabolic rate**; skip-breakfast/hunger cycles (mitochondrial fusion); get out of breath; resistance training doubles **muscle** mitochondria (with organ trade-offs).

**Never** — deficiency-responsive only (CoQ10, B12). SS31 trials mostly negative. You **can't out-eat sleep deprivation**; behavioral foundation before pills. Diet is individualized — keto/fasting life-changing for ~**20%** in trials; RCT averages hide responders.
